tagline: Along Lake Huron's north shore, then onto the ferry.
intro: From I-75 above St. Ignace, M-134 runs east as Huron Shore Drive, over the Pine River and along St. Martin Bay, through the woods to Hessel and Cedarville and past the bays and channels of the Les Cheneaux Islands. The French named the islands for those channels. There are 36 of them along 12 miles of shore.
At DeTour the land gives out. The highway goes on across the DeTour Passage by ferry and finishes on Drummond Island, one of only two Michigan highways that take a boat.
season: MDOT's byway guide names summer and fall as the best seasons.

moments.title: Hessel
moments.text: Founded in 1885 by two Swedes and a Norwegian, the town fills its public docks with the Antique Wooden Boat Show on the second weekend of August.

moments.title: DeTour Village
moments.text: Water on three sides at the eastern tip of the Upper Peninsula, where the freighters make their turn between the St. Mary's River and Lake Huron.

moments.title: Drummond Island
moments.text: The British built a fort here after the War of 1812 and gave it up once it was plain the island would be American. The island also holds alvar, a rare grassy limestone plain.

practical: The drive to Drummond Island includes the ferry crossing from DeTour, which is not counted in MDOT's drive time.
